title: Venial sin: wounds charity’s fervor without extinguishing grace or earning hell
source_text: V. Verum praeter ista peccata, docent esse quaedam peccata leviora, quae nonnihil quidem retardant hominis cursum ad Deum, & amoris Dei fervorem imminuunt; sed tamen hominem non plane a Deo avertunt, nec amorem Dei in eo extinguunt. Ac proinde per ejusmodi peccata homo non fit Deo inimicus, neque privatur vita spirituali, quoniam gratiam, quae est vitae illius principium, non excutiunt. Nec etiam talia peccata mortis aeternae reatum afferunt; sed solum poenae cujusdam temporalis: ut nec per illa homo justus justitia sua spolietur, & amittat sanctitatem illam, quae necessaria est, ut quis Deum videre possit. Adeoque quamvis mors in ejusmodi peccato hominem deprehendat, non propterea tamen est in aeternum salute excludendus, & aeternis inferni tormentis adjudicandus. Unde colligitur hujusmodi peccata esse quidem animi vulnera, sed facile curabilia; non vero morbos aut plagas lethales: Et propterea peccata, non mortalia, sed tantum venialia recte appellari.
pass_a_gloss: But besides those sins, they teach that there are certain lighter sins which indeed somewhat retard a person’s course toward God and diminish the fervor of the love of God, yet do not wholly turn the person away from God, nor extinguish the love of God in him. And therefore through sins of that kind a person does not become God’s enemy, nor is he deprived of spiritual life, because they do not cast out the grace which is the principle of that life. Nor do such sins bring the guilt of eternal death, but only of a certain temporal punishment: so that neither through them is a just person stripped of his righteousness, nor does he lose that holiness which is necessary in order that one may see God. And so although death should catch a person in a sin of that kind, he is not for that reason to be shut out forever from salvation and adjudged to the eternal torments of hell. Whence it is gathered that sins of this kind are indeed wounds of the soul, but easily curable; not truly diseases or lethal plagues: and therefore they are rightly called sins not mortal, but only venial.
pass_b_english: Lighter sins check zeal and love’s fervor without casting out grace or making God an enemy.
They merit temporal penalty only—so death in such a fault does not, of itself, damn.

choices.why: Opposed to lethal/mortal as curable wounds.
